policies.description: Any request to update a Problem must include and validate all mandatory fields required by the record.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Only users with a role that has full CRUD permissions on the Problem table (Administrator, Manager, or Agent) are allowed to perform an update on a Problem record.
references: | Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

| Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations. |

| Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. |

policies.description: When the update includes an `assigned_to` user, that user must have `users.active = true`.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.

policies.description: The update must be a single validated operation; it cannot proceed if required data is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: If a mandatory field required for the update is missing, the assistant must state which field is required instead of asking for further information.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: A Problem may be transitioned to `closed` only if there exists a linked Change Request of type `normal` or `emergency` that implements the permanent fix.
references: Final Status: A Problem transitions to closed only after the permanent fix has been successfully implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.

policies.description: If the update includes a `workaround` description, the Problem status must be set to `fix_in_progress`.
references: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.

policies.description: If the update includes a `workaround` description, the `workaround_notes` must be published to all linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.
references: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.

policies.description: When updating a Problem, ensure that all affected Incidents are linked via the `incident_to_problem` related list.
references: The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.

policies.description: Before setting a Problem’s status to `closed`, verify that all mandatory dependencies (e.g., linked Change Request) are satisfied.
references: Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.policy_name: Configuration Item Status Validation for Problem Update
policies.description: If a Problem update includes a `configuration_item` reference, the referenced Configuration Item must have `status = in_use` or `status = maintenance`. Linking a Problem to a CI with status `retired` or `disposed` is prohibited.
references: CI Status: Only CIs with status = in_use or status = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in status = retired or status = disposed.

policies.description: When updating a Problem record, the `status` field must be set to one of the allowed status values defined for problems: NEW, ASSESS, ROOT_CAUSE, FIX_IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, or CLOSED.
references:
Problem Management

  • Trigger: A Problem must be created (create_problem) when a recurring incident pattern or a major incident is identified.

  • Linking: The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.

  • Default Status: All new Problems are set to status = new.

  • Workaround: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.

  • Final Status: A Problem transitions to closed only after the permanent fix has been successfully implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.

  • Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
status: Problem status (NEW, ASSESS, ROOT_CAUSE, FIX_IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED)

policies.description: When updating a Problem, the `priority` field (if supplied) must be one of the defined priority enumeration values: critical, high, moderate, low, or planning.
references: Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.

policies.description: When updating a Problem, the `impact` field (if supplied) must be one of the allowed values: `high`, `medium`, or `low`.
references: incident.impact | high, medium, low

policies.description: When updating a Problem, the `urgency` field (if supplied) must be one of the allowed values: `high`, `medium`, or `low`.
references: incident.urgency | high, medium, low

policies.description: When updating a Problem, the `category` field (if supplied) must be one of the defined problem categories: `network`, `software`, `hardware`, or `database`.
references: category: Problem category (network, software, hardware, database).

policies.description: The `priority` of a Problem is automatically calculated by the system from the `impact` × `urgency` matrix and must not be set manually; any provided `priority` value must match the system‑derived result.
references: Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
